Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence

items.passage: B. S. Johnson’s experimental novel The Unfortunates (1969) is frequently described as lacking any fixed sequence: it was published as a box of twenty-seven separately bound sections that readers are encouraged to shuffle. ______ Johnson designated one section “First” and another “Last.” Still, the twenty-five intervening sections can be read in any order, imitating the haphazard way the narrator’s memories of a deceased friend resurface.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says the novel “is frequently described as lacking any fixed sequence.” The blank sentence then concedes a fact that limits this claim: Johnson fixed two sections in place, marking one “First” and another “Last.” The next sentence returns to the main point with “Still,” noting that “the twenty-five intervening sections can be read in any order.” “Admittedly” fits, since it introduces a point the writer grants before restating the main claim.

A.why_wrong: Fixing a first and a last section does not spell out what “lacking any fixed sequence” means; it is an exception to that claim, as the following “Still,” shows.

C.why_wrong: The box of sections that readers are encouraged to shuffle is not the reason Johnson fixed two of them in place; the fixed sections cut against the description rather than following from it.

D.why_wrong: The fixed first and last sections are not a further point in support of the claim that the novel can be read in any order; they are a limit on it, which “Still,” then sets aside.

items.notes: Grant then turn on the 3.19 / f5959727 shape (claim, concession in the blank sentence, Still resumes), keyed Admittedly to spread K1 keys (7 of 13 live K1 items key Of course). items.subtype: Concession: qualification of a supported claim
items.passage: Ice cores extracted from Antarctica preserve samples of Earth’s ancient atmosphere: as accumulating snow is compressed into glacial ice, it encloses minuscule air bubbles whose carbon dioxide concentrations researchers can measure. ______ the bubbles seal only once the snow lies buried tens of meters deep, often centuries after it fell, so the air in any layer is younger than the surrounding ice.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says that ice cores “preserve samples of Earth’s ancient atmosphere” in “minuscule air bubbles.” The blank sentence then adds a fact that limits how directly that record can be read: “the bubbles seal only once the snow lies buried tens of meters deep,” so “the air in any layer is younger than the surrounding ice.” “That said” fits, since it introduces a qualification of the preceding claim.

A.why_wrong: The value of ice cores as an atmospheric record does not cause the bubbles to seal late; the late sealing is a separate fact that limits that record.

B.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not add another strength of ice cores; it points out that the trapped air is “younger than the surrounding ice,” a limit on the record.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence is not a rewording of how ice traps air; it adds new information (the depth at which bubbles seal and the age gap that results) that qualifies the first claim.

items.notes: Qualification of a supported claim (3.12 / ecb31049 shape: a strength, then a fact that limits it). Band 6 by plan. Concession key, so no contrast decoy and no In fact, Indeed or Actually. Trap: In other words and Furthermore for a reader who takes the first half of the blank sentence (how bubbles seal) as more detail on the trapping process; the limit arrives only in the so clause. Real subject (the gas-age / ice-age difference in ice cores) described from general knowledge, no researcher named. items.passage: Ming dynasty potters in Jingdezhen decorated their porcelain with cobalt pigment, which turns blue during firing. Chemical analyses indicate that the cobalt used throughout the fifteenth century did not all originate from a single source; ______ early in the century, artisans relied on ore imported from Persia, rich in iron but poor in manganese, whereas later pieces increasingly employed domestic ore with the reverse composition.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The clause before the blank says that the cobalt “did not all originate from a single source.” The clause after it names those sources: “ore imported from Persia” early in the century and “domestic ore” later. “Specifically” fits, since the second clause gives the exact content of the general claim before it.

B.why_wrong: The clause after the blank contains its own contrast (Persian ore early, “whereas” local ore later), but it does not oppose the clause before the blank; it spells out the claim that the cobalt “did not all originate from a single source.”

C.why_wrong: The use of Persian and then domestic ore is not a result of what the chemical analyses indicate; it is what the analyses found.

D.why_wrong: The clause after the blank is not a further, separate finding; it identifies the sources that the clause before the blank says the cobalt came from.

items.passage: Among the Dogon people of Mali, village disputes are traditionally settled in the toguna, an open-sided shelter where men assemble to deliberate. Villagers want such discussions to remain peaceable. ______ they rest the toguna’s heavy roof of stacked millet stalks on pillars so short that no one can stand upright beneath it; a man who leaps up in anger strikes his head.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence states a goal: “Villagers want such discussions to remain peaceable.” The blank sentence describes what the villagers do to serve that goal: “they rest the toguna’s heavy roof of stacked millet stalks on pillars so short that no one can stand upright beneath it,” so “a man who leaps up in anger strikes his head.” “To that end” fits, since it introduces an action taken to achieve the aim just stated.

A.why_wrong: Resting the roof on short pillars is not a rewording of the wish to keep discussions peaceable; it is a separate action taken to serve that wish.

B.why_wrong: The low roof does not oppose the aim of keeping discussions peaceable; it works toward it by stopping anyone from rising in anger.

C.why_wrong: Building the roof low is not just one more fact about the toguna; the villagers do it as the means of keeping disputes peaceable.

items.passage: Maria Firmina dos Reis’s Úrsula (1859) ranks among the earliest antislavery novels written in Brazil. Dos Reis published it under a pseudonym, however, and in the provincial city of São Luís, distant from the literary establishment of Rio de Janeiro. ______ for about a century the novel was overlooked by literary historians, even as subsequent antislavery novels by better-known writers were widely celebrated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence explains why the novel was easy to miss: Dos Reis “published it under a pseudonym” and in a city “distant from the literary establishment of Rio de Janeiro.” The blank sentence gives the result of that obscure publication: “for about a century the novel was overlooked by literary historians.” “Accordingly” fits, since it introduces a consequence of the circumstances just described.

A.why_wrong: The neglect of the novel does not qualify or cut against the fact that it was published under a pseudonym far from the literary capital; it follows from it. The contrast with the novel’s standing today has already been marked by “however.”

C.why_wrong: The century of neglect is not an instance of the novel’s obscure publication; it is what that publication led to.

D.why_wrong: The blank sentence does not add a separate fact about how the novel was published; it states the outcome of those circumstances.

items.notes: Band-7 E1 move on the f5a00eff architecture: a claim, a qualifying sentence with however, then the consequence of that qualification. items.passage: On a single beech tree, leaves developing in full sunlight at the top of the canopy are typically small and thick, containing several layers of photosynthetic cells. Leaves in the shaded interior, ______ are expansive and thin, maximizing the surface available to intercept the scarce illumination that filters through.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes sun leaves as “small and thick.” The second describes shade leaves on the same tree, which “are expansive and thin.” “By contrast” fits, since it marks the second kind of leaf as the opposite of the first on the same features.

A.why_wrong: Shade leaves are not an instance of the sun leaves just described; they are a second kind of leaf with the opposite shape.

B.why_wrong: The second sentence does not reword the description of sun leaves; it describes different leaves, which are “expansive and thin” rather than “small and thick.”

D.why_wrong: Shade leaves are not like sun leaves; being “expansive and thin” is the reverse of being “small and thick.”

items.notes: Two subjects, opposite values, connective as an interrupter after the second subject (2.6 shape). items.passage: Investigations of hatchling behavior have established that newly emerged sea turtles locate the ocean by crawling toward the brightest portion of the horizon, which on an undeveloped beach is the open sky above the water. ______ numerous Florida coastal communities require beachfront lighting to be shielded or dimmed throughout nesting season, so that hatchlings are not lured inland.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence reports a finding: hatchlings “locate the ocean by crawling toward the brightest portion of the horizon.” The blank sentence describes rules made in light of that finding: lighting must be “shielded or dimmed throughout nesting season, so that hatchlings are not lured inland.” “Accordingly” fits, since it introduces an action taken in keeping with the information before it.
